source: NCERT-aligned UPSC Ecology & Environment (Class XI), Ch. 4 (Wildlife Conservation and Protected Areas of India).

sections.heading: 1. Conservation — In-situ and Ex-situ
points: **In-situ conservation** — protecting species in their **natural habitat** (National Parks, Sanctuaries, Biosphere Reserves).
**Ex-situ conservation** — protecting species **outside their habitat** (zoos, botanical gardens, gene/seed banks, captive breeding).
The legal basis is the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**.

sections.heading: 2. Protected Area Categories
points: **National Park** — highly protected; no human activity/grazing/private rights allowed; boundaries fixed by law.
**Wildlife Sanctuary** — protected, but certain regulated human activities (grazing, collection) may be permitted; focused on species.
**Biosphere Reserve** — large areas with a **core (strictly protected), buffer, and transition zone**; integrate conservation with sustainable use; part of UNESCO's MAB programme.
**Conservation and Community Reserves** — buffer/community-managed areas (added in 2002 amendment).

sections.heading: 3. Species-Specific Projects
points: **Project Tiger (1973)** — tiger reserves; India has the largest tiger population.
**Project Elephant (1992)** — elephant reserves and corridors.
Programmes for the **Gangetic dolphin (national aquatic animal), one-horned rhino (Kaziranga), Asiatic lion (Gir), Great Indian Bustard, vultures, snow leopard**.
National animal = **tiger**; national aquatic animal = **Gangetic dolphin**; national bird = **peacock**.

sections.heading: 4. Key Protected Areas
points: **Kaziranga (Assam)** — one-horned rhino; **Gir (Gujarat)** — Asiatic lion; **Sundarbans (WB)** — Royal Bengal tiger, mangroves.
**Jim Corbett (Uttarakhand)** — first national park (and first Tiger Reserve); **Periyar (Kerala)**; **Ranthambore (Rajasthan)**; **Nilgiri, Nanda Devi = Biosphere Reserves**.
India has 18 Biosphere Reserves, 50+ Tiger Reserves, 100+ National Parks.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: In-situ = in natural habitat (parks, sanctuaries, biosphere reserves); ex-situ = zoos, gene banks.
Biosphere Reserve zones: core, buffer, transition.
Project Tiger (1973); Project Elephant (1992).
Kaziranga = one-horned rhino; Gir = Asiatic lion; Sundarbans = Royal Bengal tiger.
National aquatic animal = Gangetic dolphin; Corbett = first national park.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **In-situ = in the natural habitat**; **ex-situ = outside it** (zoos, gene banks).
A **National Park is more strictly protected** than a Wildlife Sanctuary.
**Biosphere Reserve zones = core, buffer, transition**.
**Project Tiger = 1973; Project Elephant = 1992** (do not swap).
